thread:
sofia_support: Customer reported a build break after upgrading to our tagged v2.0.1 release. They say `go get` fails with a module path mismatch. sending logs.

sofia_support: repro steps from customer:
1) git clone their app
2) in app root `GO111MODULE=on go mod tidy`
3) `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.1`

sofia_support: error they pasted:
```
go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.1: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.1: reading github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/go.mod at revision v2.0.1: module declares its path as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2
	but was required as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk
```

evan_eng: :eyes: that error is the classic v2 module path mismatch. Do we have the v2.0.1 tag metadata handy? did release pipeline alter go.mod accidentally?

michael_release: deploy-bot: release pipeline shows v2.0.1 created from branch release/v2, but CI logs show we cherry-picked changes and forgot to update module path in the source branch before tagging. go.mod in the v2 tag still had `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` instead of `/v2`.

ejan_eng: (typo, corrected) evan_eng: ok confirmed. Root cause: tag is semver v2+, but module path in go.mod wasn't updated to include /v2. That causes `go` to detect a mismatch when a consumer requests the module without the /v2 suffix.

julie_cs: Customer is blocked in CI; they use a private proxy and `replace` directives to point at our fork sometimes. Any short-term workaround we can offer them while we cut a fix release?

evan_eng: Short-term workarounds (consumer side):
- If they can use `GOPROXY=direct` and `go get` a local copy: `GOPROXY=direct go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.1` might still fail because the module file inside the tag is wrong.
- Best quick workaround: vendor the SDK or switch to the v1 import path until we publish a corrected v2 tag.
- Another hack: ask them to `replace` the module in their go.mod to point to a local patched clone that has `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` in go.mod. Example:
```
replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk => ../local/go-sdk
```
and in ../local/go-sdk/go.mod set `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` and `go 1.20` then `go mod tidy` in their app.
```
That requires local editing on their side, not ideal.

michael_release: We'll cut v2.0.2 ASAP with corrected go.mod and run a short verification matrix (go1.19-1.21, proxy=direct, goproxy=proxy). ETA ~2 hours. I'll do the tag and a follow-up post here.

julie_cs: Customer asked if this could cause upstream transitive dependency surprises when they have other modules requiring v1 vs v2. They are worried about replace + private proxy combos.

evan_eng: Yes, when a module path mismatches you can see strange resolution behavior. If someone `require`s `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` (no /v2) and we have a v2 tag with wrong go.mod, the go tool can't reconcile. That is likely why their CI fails intermittently when cache/proxy state changes. The proper fix is to ensure the module path in the new v2 tag ends with `/v2` and consumers update imports to `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`.

sofia_support: passing this to customer: we'll provide a few options: 1) vendor the SDK, 2) apply local replace to a patched clone, or 3) wait ~2h for v2.0.2. They asked if we can make the release a patch with no code changes except go.mod to minimize risk.

michael_release: yes, v2.0.2 will be a go.mod-only fix. I'm going to create the tag now, trigger CI, and mark the release notes as "module path fix for v2 compatibility". will post the new tag sha here when done.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered for tag v2.0.2 (job 4821). status: queued -> running.

evan_eng: after the tag is published, customers behind private proxies might need to purge caches or set GOPROXY=direct temporarily. We'll include a recommended snippet:
```
# purge cache and get new tag directly
GOPROXY=direct go clean -modcache
go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2@v2.0.2
```

julie_cs: Customer appreciates quick turnaround. they're going to hold CI for ~3 hours. I'll update them once we confirm the tag and provide the SHA + verification steps.

michael_release: done — tag v2.0.2 pushed: sha: 8c3b9d7. CI passed on go1.20 and go1.21.

sofia_support: passing to customer: v2.0.2 is available (sha 8c3b9d7). Recommend they run the purge + `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2@v2.0.2` and confirm. If they still use replace/pri proxies we'll help with cache purge steps.

julie_cs: :thumbsup: closing loop with customer in 30m unless they report further errors.

evan_eng: note for team — adding an automated check to our release pipeline to ensure module path matches major tag for v2+ (fail CI if mismatch). I'll file a tiny issue after this thread.

sofia_support: thanks all, moving thread to resolved after confirmation from customer.
